# City Research Solutions

> A full-service consumer research firm in the Madison, Wisconsin area, established in 1979. Focus groups, surveys, ethnographies, retail and quantitative research, in person and online, with its own research facility in Janesville, Wisconsin. Pervasive Insights (pervasiveinsights.ai) is its AI suite.

## Research services
- [In-facility research](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/capabilities-in-facility): focus groups, central location tests, in-depth interviews.
- [Online research](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/capabilities-online): online groups, bulletin boards, surveys, panels, in-home tests.
- [Real-time research](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/capabilities-real-time): diaries, ethnographies, in-home usage testing.
- [Retail research](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/capabilities-retail): shop-alongs, packaging, point-of-purchase, simulated shopping.
- [Quantitative research](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/capabilities-quantitative): conjoint, TURF, pricing, factor and decision-tree analysis.
- [Research facilities](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/facilities): focus group rooms, viewing suites and a test kitchen in Janesville, WI.

## Guides
- [What to re-field in a tracking programme, and how often](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/what-to-refield-and-how-often): a refresh ladder for brand, purchase, price and segmentation measures, and where tracking budgets are usually wasted.
- [Pricing research is more than one question](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/pricing-research-methods): how Van Westendorp and Gabor Granger work together, extending Van Westendorp to read share lost to expensiveness, and three methods that round out a pricing study (Newton Miller Smith, monadic price cells, brand price trade-off).
- [Three ways to watch a competitor](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/competitive-monitoring): Three ways to watch a competitor: how social listening, a competitive shelf sweep and a purchase diary answer different questions at different speeds, with an interactive sample dashboard built on fictional brands.
- [Custom research communities](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/research-communities): Custom research communities: a sample quarterly report for a B2B technician community and a consumer home baker community, with recruitment funnel, 12-week engagement, activities run, turnaround vs fresh recruiting, member quotes, decisions and cost per question over a year.
- [Which Idea Should You Build?](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/concept-testing): Concept testing as the first gate in new product development: how CRS screens early ideas with a monadic test against a benchmark and norm band, how results feed the development roadmap and later gates (renderings, prototypes, home use tests), with a sample readout for a fictional frozen meal brand.
- [Testing a Package Before It Ships](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/packaging-research): Packaging and claims test example, online and in person: shelf find time and rate, first-click attention heat maps, an in-person shelf layout test with eye-tracking glasses (gaze heat and spotlight maps, package-level eye-track scores), and claim appeal, believability and TURF reach for a fictional sparkling water brand, n=450 across three designs.
- [Segmentation, Brought to Life](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/market-segmentation): Next-generation segmentation: segments built from a survey of real category buyers, then brought to life as an AI-driven synthetic panel calibrated to each segment (one-on-one chat, panel survey, focus groups), plus sizing by people and dollars, needs, brand share, where to play and a typing tool (fictional home fitness example).
- [What a Taste Test Misses](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/in-home-use-test): In-home use test example: sequential monadic design, 9-point and just-about-right ballot, penalty analysis, week-by-week liking and usage with video diaries, and a launch recommendation (fictional plant-based yogurt).
- [Focus Groups, Start to Finish](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/focus-groups): Focus groups, start to finish: a sample screener with quota logic, a 90-minute discussion guide with quiet before and after ballots to offset group bias, a topline report and deliverables for a fictional frozen pizza brand.
- [Examples of our work](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/examples): generic, fully fictional examples of City Research Solutions deliverables.
- [Inside a Blind Taste Test](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/taste-test): Central location taste and sensory test example: blind, rotated (sequential monadic) tasting of three recipes by 150 category buyers in a focus facility, 9-point and just-about-right ballot, a trained panel attribute profile, penalty analysis, preference share by buyer group and a recommendation (fictional kettle chip brand cutting sodium).
- [Can They Build It From the Box?](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/assembly-testing): Instructions and assembly testing example: 20 buyers assemble a flat-pack product in our facility while observed and timed, with task success, time and errors by step, where people got stuck, a page-by-page instruction heat map, rewrite recommendations and a before and after retest with 20 new builders (fictional standing desk brand).
- [One-on-One Interviews at Survey Scale](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/ai-moderated-interviews): AI-moderated interviews example: a senior researcher writes the guide and probe rules, an AI moderator runs 180 one-on-one text and voice interviews with follow-up probes, and the researcher reviews transcripts and writes the readout, with a sample guide, transcript excerpt, themes with counts and quotes, and when to choose AI-moderated or human-moderated (fictional reusable water bottle brand).
- [A Focus Group That Takes Its Time](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/online-bulletin-boards): Online bulletin board example: 24 stick vacuum owners over four days with a day-by-day activity plan, group, private and private-first questions, a sample thread with moderator probes, concept markup hotspots, coded themes with quotes and deliverables (fictional cordless vacuum brand).
- [The Purchase Nobody Remembers](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/experience-diary): Path-to-purchase experience diary example: 40 shoppers log 1,284 phone entries over 21 days from first need to first use, with a journey map by stage, the moments that moved people toward or away, days from trigger to purchase, where the brand was missing and sample entries (fictional air fryer brand).
- [Watching the Real Routine](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/virtual-ethnography): Virtual ethnography example: 12 live video home visits during weeknight dinner cleanup plus follow-up tasks, with a household roster, what people said compared with what they did, a workaround photo log, themes with opportunity areas and a time-stamped highlight reel (fictional dish care brand).
- [What Shoppers Do at the Shelf](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/shop-along): Shop-along and point-of-purchase interview example: 24 accompanied trips (18 in store, 6 online by screen share) plus 120 shelf intercepts, with shopper roster, aisle path and time at the shelf, look to pick-up to purchase funnel by brand, decision moments, said vs did, and ranked shelf fixes (fictional sparkling energy drink).
- [Which Features, Which Flavors?](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/conjoint-turf): Choice-based conjoint and TURF example: feature importance, part-worths, value of each upgrade in cents, a what-if share of preference simulator, and an interactive flavor line-up builder showing reach and overlap, for a fictional protein bar brand with 800 buyers and fictional test price levels.
- [Every Study You Own, Searchable](https://cityresearchsolutions.com/research-library): Pervasive Insights research library example: 12 fictional past studies (2016 to 2025) searchable in plain language, with answers citing study, year and sample, a topic coverage map, evidence and freshness scores, and flags for when to field new research, alongside calibrated synthetic panels.
